# A painted SharedWorker example times out while the landing-cover camera waits for network idle

## Context

The [landing cover producer](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/37d39d6e74/buildScripts/docs/captureExamples.mjs) captures the actual first frame without per-example recipes. During #21915, its dark and light passes both expired while the three charts were visible and usable. The same command against the already merged `dashboard-sortable` example expired in both palettes too.

## The Problem

With the dev server running, use `npm run capture-examples -- --record dashboard-sortable --base-url http://localhost:8080/ --output-dir <new-empty-directory>`. On Chromium in this run, `landingReady` timed out at its 15-second Playwright `networkidle` wait. The page reported `load` before the timeout. On the shared-planning example a 20-second request trace had three unfinished Playwright script requests, for the App, Data and VDom workers. All three URLs matched real, live CDP SharedWorker targets. Other HTTP assets had finished; both viewport and document had the requested palette, all eight tasks were visible, and the same page completed the real cross-window drag.

## The Fix

Distinguish a live SharedWorker startup request from a genuinely pending page resource when establishing landing readiness. Keep the existing downstream mounted-view, correct-palette, settled-DOM and painted-resource checks. Implement the rule in the common producer. An unknown pending request must remain distinguishable in a failure diagnostic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The actual CLI captures both palettes on a SharedWorker example without a recipe, input steps or a fixed sleep. Verify distinct files and the reported palette with the example still using SharedWorkers.
- [ ] A deliberately held ordinary HTTP request still prevents a false settled capture. The mounted-view, wrong-scheme and changing-DOM controls retain their existing behavior.
- [ ] A standard single-window example still produces both images. Record the observed worker targets and the treatment of requests at failure without embedding test instructions in a Portal record.

## Related

#21903 and #21933 delivered the landing and pairing paths. #21915 supplies the three-window consumer. The new example's independently captured real opening frames are available for this cut. The issue owns the stock CLI's behavior. Current open-queue sweep and all-state searches for network idle, landing and SharedWorker capture found no existing owner.
